properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-20, choosing between three placements that were each simulated against reflow2's real import graph before any was proposed. All three removed the cycle equally, so the choice was about what the boxes MEAN, not about correctness.

THE CHOICE: a NINTH system, sys:foundation, holding cmp:nodes, cmp:schema, cmp:graph, cmp:provenance and cmp:identity. sys:store keeps cmp:export and cmp:search. sys:vocabulary keeps cmp:flow and cmp:vocabulary.

THE TWO REJECTED OPTIONS, recorded so the reasoning is not re-run:
  · fold the kernel into sys:store - fewest moving parts, stays at eight systems, but nodes and schema ARE the vocabulary, so a system called Vocabulary would hold neither of them. A name that no longer describes its contents is the same class of defect being fixed.
  · fold the kernel into sys:vocabulary - the mirror image. The graph and store-access layer ends up under a name that describes it no better.

WHY A NEW SYSTEM IS THE HONEST ANSWER: the five modules are mutually dependent, so they ARE one layer - that is the whole finding. Neither existing name covers all five, and forcing one to is how the model became misleading in the first place. Naming the layer says the true thing; folding it into a neighbour hides a layer inside a box named for something else.

ACCEPTED COST: two systems end up with two components each. Small boxes are not a defect.
properties.name: The kernel is its own system — sys:foundation, because neither 'store' nor 'vocabulary' describes all five of the modules everything sits on
properties.rationale:
This is a change to the CARVING, not to the arithmetic, and that distinction is why it is a decision of its own rather than another correction on dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition. When that decision went from seven systems to eight it was catching up with a system that already existed; here a system is being created because the coupling says the layer exists and the model never named it.

It does not overturn dec:bl83a. That decision's principle - reflow2's own decomposition is the functional systems a design-graph tool IS, not its file tree - is what makes this move correct: a design-graph tool fundamentally IS a typed store of identified nodes, and that is one function, not two.

THE EVIDENCE, measured rather than argued: nodes is transitively depended on by 46 of 52 core modules, provenance by 44, identity by 44, schema by 43, graph by 42. See fact:the-modules-are-acyclic-but-the-declared-subsystems-are-not for the cycle this bisection produced and fact:ten-components-report-a-zero-blast-radius-the-source-contradicts for cmp:identity, which was in no system at all while 44 modules stood on it.
